files.lesson.md: --- order: 2 unit: expressions node: AC9M7A01 n2 title: Substituting into formulas summary: To use a formula, replace each letter with its value, write in the × signs, then work it out in the right order. language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A formula is a recipe for a number. Put in the values you know, and it gives you the one you want: a perimeter, a cost, a speed." connection: forecast-fahrenheit # data/connections/maths.yml (documentation only) app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8143 url: http://127.0.0.1:8143/index.html readySelector: "#sl-l" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: formula.yml#pic, caption: "$l = 5$ and $w = 3$: write in the × signs, $P = 2 \\times 5 + 2 \\times 3 = 10 + 6 = 16$ cm." } explainClip: query: { code: "@formula.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Replace each letter with its value" say: "To use a formula, replace each letter with its value." clip: - caption: { text: "P = 2l + 2w, with l = 3 and w = 2.", say: "P equals two l plus two w, with l as three and w as two." } - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "2l means 2 × l: write in the × signs.", say: "Two l means two times l, so write in the times signs." } - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "2 × 3 + 2 × 2 = 6 + 4 = 10 cm.", say: "Two times three, plus two times two, is six plus four: ten." } - click: Make l bigger - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "New values, same formula: 2 × 4 + 2 × 2 = 12 cm.", say: "New values, same formula: two times four plus two times two is twelve." } - expect: { selector: ".rulework", contains: "P = 2 × 4 + 2 × 2 = 12" } - wait: 1200 --- To **substitute** into a formula is to replace each letter with its value, then work out the answer. ## Predict: a perimeter ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a value exposes reading 2l with l = 5 as 25, the digits side by side." check: type: predict q: "$P = 2l + 2w$. What is $P$ when $l = 5$ and $w = 3$?" options: ["16", "13", "30", "48"] actual: "16. 2l means 2 × l = 2 × 5 = 10, and 2w = 2 × 3 = 6. So P = 10 + 6 = 16. (48 comes from reading 2l as 25 and 2w as 23.)" ``` $$P = 2l + 2w$$ What does $2l$ mean here? ## Run: check your value ```step stage: run insight: "The board writes every substitution out with the × signs, so the student can compare it with their own working." try: { playground: board, starter: "formula.yml#run", height: 520 } check: { type: board, text: "Set $l = 5$ and $w = 3$. Was your prediction right?", when: "l = 5 and w = 3" } ``` Read the working under the rectangle. Where did the × signs come from? A number written next to a letter, such as $2l$, means multiply: $2 \times l$. ## Investigate: three steps ```step stage: investigate insight: "Substituting is three steps: write the formula, replace each letter (with × signs in), then work out in order: multiply before adding." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "The area of a rectangle is $A = lw$. Find $A$ when $l = 8$ and $w = 3$." answer: "24" feedback: - ["83", "lw means l × w. Put the numbers in with a × sign between them."] - ["11", "lw means l × w, not l + w."] explain: "A = 8 × 3 = 24." - check: type: answer q: "A plumber charges $C = 5h + 20$ dollars. Find $C$ when $h = 3$." answer: "35" feedback: - ["75", "That adds first: 5 × (3 + 20). Multiply first, then add: 5 × 3 + 20."] - ["73", "5h means 5 × h, not 5 then 3."] - ["15", "That is the hours only. Add the 20."] explain: "C = 5 × 3 + 20 = 15 + 20 = 35 dollars." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#leo" text: "Leo works out a perimeter. Click the line where he goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: algebra-juxtaposition explain: "Line 2: 2l means 2 × l, so 2 × 5 = 10, not 25. With the × signs in: P = 2 × 5 + 2 × 3 = 10 + 6 = 16." ``` ### Area Here is how to substitute, step by step. ```worked P = 2l + 2w :: Write the formula first. l = 5, \; w = 3 :: Write down the values you know. P = 2 \times 5 + 2 \times 3 :: Replace each letter with its value. Write in the × signs that were hidden in $2l$ and $2w$. P = 10 + 6 :: Multiply before adding. P = 16 \text{ cm} :: Add, and give the units. ``` ### A plumber ### Find the mistake Read Leo's working one line at a time. What does $2l$ mean? ## Modify: other formulas ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a decimal value, three letters multiplied, a division, and brackets that are worked out first." try: { playground: board, starter: "formula.yml#decimal", height: 520 } tasks: - starter: "formula.yml#decimal" check: type: answer q: "Find $P = 2l + 2w$ when $l = 2.5$ and $w = 4$. Set the board to check your substitution." answer: "13" feedback: - ["25", "2l is 2 × 2.5 = 5, not 2 then 2.5."] - ["8.5", "That adds l and w once each. There are two of each."] explain: "P = 2 × 2.5 + 2 × 4 = 5 + 8 = 13 cm." - starter: "formula.yml#box" check: type: answer q: "The volume of a box is $V = lwh$. Find $V$ when $l = 2$, $w = 3$ and $h = 4$." answer: "24" feedback: - ["9", "lwh means l × w × h, not l + w + h."] - ["234", "lwh means multiply: put × signs between the values."] explain: "V = 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 cubic units." - starter: "formula.yml#speed" check: type: answer q: "Average speed is $s = d / t$ (distance ÷ time). Find $s$ in km/h when $d = 120$ km and $t = 2$ hours." answer: "60" feedback: - ["240", "d / t means d ÷ t. Divide, don't multiply."] explain: "s = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h." - starter: "formula.yml#brackets" check: type: answer q: "A hire company charges $C = 5(h + 4)$ dollars. Find $C$ when $h = 2$." answer: "30" feedback: - ["14", "That is 5 × 2 + 4. The brackets are worked out first: 2 + 4, then × 5."] - ["56", "5(h + 4) means 5 × (h + 4). Put h = 2 in the brackets first."] explain: "C = 5 × (2 + 4) = 5 × 6 = 30 dollars." ``` ### A decimal Each task loads a new formula. The board shows the substitution, but not the answer: work it out yourself. ### Three letters ### Divide ### Brackets ## Practise: substitute ```step stage: practise insight: "Substituting into new formulas with the order of operations, mixed; the review is naming variables and constants from the last lesson." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Find $T = 12n + 6$ when $n = 4$." answer: "54" feedback: - ["130", "12n with n = 4 is 12 × 4, not 124. Then add 6."] - ["120", "That adds first. Multiply 12 × 4, then add 6."] explain: "T = 12 × 4 + 6 = 48 + 6 = 54." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "$12n$ means 12 times $n$. What's $12n$ when $n = 4$?", answer: 48, explain: "12 × 4 = 48. Now add the 6." } - check: type: answer q: "Find $y = 3(x - 2)$ when $x = 7$." answer: "15" feedback: - ["19", "That is 3 × 7 − 2. Work out the brackets first: 7 − 2."] explain: "y = 3 × (7 − 2) = 3 × 5 = 15." - check: type: answer q: "Find $A = \\frac{bh}{2}$ (the area of a triangle) when $b = 6$ and $h = 5$." answer: "15" feedback: - ["30", "That is b × h. The formula then divides by 2."] - ["5.5", "bh means b × h, not b + h."] explain: "A = 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15." - check: type: question q: "Review: in $V = 3t + 10$, which are the constants?" options: ["3 and 10", "$V$ and $t$", "Only 10"] answer: 0 explain: "3 and 10 stay the same; V and t are variables that change." ``` ### Tickets ### Brackets again ### A triangle ### Review ## Make: rectangles with the same area ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing values to hit a target reverses substitution: from the answer back to the letters." try: { playground: board, starter: "formula.yml#make", height: 520 } hint: ["A = l × w. Which two whole numbers multiply to 24?", "Try l = 6. What must w be?"] check: { type: board, text: "Make a rectangle with an area of 24 cm².", when: "A = 24", explain: "Your l × w = 24. Other pairs work too: 3 × 8, 4 × 6, 2 × 12." } ``` Find a rectangle with area 24 cm². Then find another one. How many can you find with whole-number sides? Stretch: which of your rectangles has the smallest perimeter? Use $P = 2l + 2w$ to check. ## Make: °F to °C, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A US forecast gives °F, and the conversion formula has brackets, a multiplication and a division. Writing the substituted line and working the brackets first shows whether the order holds up." hint: ["Replace F with 86 and keep the brackets.", "Work out the brackets first: 86 − 32."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A US weather forecast says 86 °F. The formula for degrees Celsius is $C = (F - 32) \\times 5 \\div 9$. What is the temperature in °C?" steps: - ["$C = (F - 32) \\times 5 \\div 9$, with $F = 86$", "write the formula and the value"] - ["$C = (86 - 32) \\times 5 \\div 9$", "replace $F$ with its value and keep the brackets"] - ["$= 54 \\times 5 \\div 9$", "brackets first: $86 - 32 = 54$"] - ["$= 270 \\div 9 = 30$ °C", "then multiply and divide, left to right"] - ["30 °C is a hot day, and 86 °F is a hot day too", "does the answer make sense?"] picks: - step: 3 q: "What do you work out first in $(86 - 32) \\times 5 \\div 9$?" options: - "The brackets: $86 - 32$" - "The multiplication: $32 \\times 5$" - "The division: $5 \\div 9$" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The 32 is inside the brackets with the 86. Work out the brackets first.", "Brackets come before division."] answer: "30" tolerance: 0 answerLabel: "Temperature (°C)" feedback: - ["68.2", "That does $32 \\times 5 \\div 9$ before the brackets. Work out $86 - 32$ first."] - ["54", "That stops after the brackets. The formula then multiplies by 5 and divides by 9."] criteria: - "I wrote the formula, then the substituted line with the brackets kept." - "I worked out the brackets before multiplying and dividing." - "My answer makes sense for a hot day." explain: "$(86 - 32) \\times 5 \\div 9 = 54 \\times 5 \\div 9 = 270 \\div 9 = 30$, so 86 °F is 30 °C. The formula is exact." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. Write the formula, the line with 86 in place of $F$, then the arithmetic one step at a time, and type the temperature. **Also used in** - **Weather abroad.** US forecasts and ovens use °F. The conversion formula turns them into °C, once you put the value in. - **Ladders and scoreboards.** A rule like points $= 3W + D$ gives every team's points when you put in their wins and draws. - **Checking answers.** Every equation you solve later is checked by substituting the answer back in. ```teacher summary: Students substitute values into formulas, writing in the hidden × signs and using the order of operations, including decimals, division and brackets (AC9M7A01, node 2). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min struggle: Seeing that 2l means 2 × l, then doing the multiplying before the adding, and the brackets before both. Ask for the formula written with the × signs in before any arithmetic. goals: - I can replace each letter in a formula with its value, writing in the × signs. - I can work out the result in the right order, including brackets and division. - I can show my substitution as a line of working, with units. before: > Do the Modify boards yourself first: they show the substitution but hide the value, so students must finish the arithmetic. The new move is writing the hidden × signs. The common error is reading 2l with l = 5 as 25 (Leo's mistake). Insist on a line of working with × signs, every time, before any arithmetic. The Run board shows the full working, so students can compare it with their own line. running: - "Predict: show of hands. Ask a student who chose 48 how they got it, then write 2l = 2 × l on the board." - "Run: have students say the board's working line aloud: 'two times five plus two times three'." - "Investigate: model the worked example live. Write the formula, the values, then the substituted line, before any arithmetic." - "Modify: before brackets, ask what 5(h + 4) means in words." - "Make: collect every rectangle the class found with area 24. Is there a pattern?" - "Paper: the °F to °C task is worked in books; the page marks the answer (30) and the reason for working the brackets first. Books out, and look for the substituted line with the brackets kept." stuck: - see: A student writes digits side by side (25 for 2l with l = 5). ask: What sign is hiding between the 2 and the l? fix: Write the formula again with every × sign in, then substitute. - see: A student adds before multiplying (5 × 3 + 20 = 75). ask: "Which do you do first: multiply or add?" fix: Multiply and divide before adding and subtracting, unless brackets say otherwise. stretch: Find P = 2l + 2w and A = lw for l = 4.5 and w = 2. Find a rectangle where P and A are the same number. support: "Give a template with three lines: formula, substituted (with × signs), answer with units." leads: > Next: finding an unknown, where the answer is known and one letter is not. Substitution is also how every solution is checked, in Equations and in Linear relations (tables from rules). exit: q: Find C = 8h + 15 when h = 3, and V = lwh when l = 2, w = 5, h = 3. a: C = 8 × 3 + 15 = 39. V = 2 × 5 × 3 = 30. explain: > To **substitute**, replace each letter with its value. A number next to a letter means multiply: $2l$ means $2 \times l$. Two letters next to each other also multiply: $lw$ means $l \times w$. Write the × signs in before working anything out. Then work it out in order: brackets first, then × and ÷, then + and −. Give the units. ```
